A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BiTrajDiff research. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison, including v3's Appendices A-H. v2 ends with references and has no appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original D4RL locomotion experiments using IQL and TD3BC, plus measurements of generated-trajectory accuracy and diversity.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds navigation, manipulation, additional learner evaluations, and component and sensitivity studies.

M1.justification: The stated likelihood objective in Eq. 2 changes from minimizing log likelihood to minimizing negative log likelihood. This is a limited objective correction: the denoising loss in Eq. 4, bidirectional generation, anchor stitching, trajectory completion, and both filters remain unchanged. The newly documented architecture does not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: v3 retains the nine locomotion settings and adds Maze2D umaze/medium/large, AntMaze umaze/medium/large-diverse, and Franka Kitchen complete/partial/mixed evaluations (Tables 2 and S3). These substantially extend coverage to navigation and manipulation.

E2.justification: Tables S2-S3 add CQL and Decision Transformer evaluations, including unaugmented baselines compared with their BiTrajDiff-augmented counterparts, beyond v2's IQL and TD3BC. The three competing augmentation methods—RTDiff, Synther, and DiffStitch—are retained.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs vary the critic's n-step TD estimator over n = 2, 5, 10, and 15 and the augmentation ratio over 0%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, and 100%. v3 also evaluates additional learner and component configurations. Appendix B's newly disclosed default settings do not establish changes to previously reported experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds downstream-return ablations of generation direction, separate and combined trajectory filters, augmentation-ratio sensitivity, and n-step TD sensitivity (Sections 5.3-5.4; Appendices D-G). v2's accuracy/diversity analysis is retained as v3 Figure 6; it is distinct from these new tests.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly report standard deviations over five random seeds. v3 extends uncertainty displays to additional results without establishing a changed run count, new confidence-interval procedure, or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds benchmark and ablation results throughout Table 2 and Appendices C-G. Numerous retained Table 1 entries also change: IQL hopper-medium RTDiff changes from 78.8 ± 6.0 to 62.0 ± 2.4, and IQL hopper-medium-expert Base changes from 90.4 ± 12.8 to 105.4 ± 6.3. BiTrajDiff's Table 1 task scores remain unchanged. These are reported revisions, not established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Eq. 2 corrects the mathematical optimization direction by adding the missing minus sign before log likelihood. The remaining mathematical development is essentially retained; combining v2's stitching Eqs. 5-6 into v3's Eq. 5 is equivalent restatement. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of novel bidirectional augmentation, connectivity between previously unconnected states, greater behavioral diversity, and improved D4RL performance across offline RL learners. The expanded experiments support these existing claims without redefining the core contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of filter benefits, sparse-reward performance, and generation direction. It also attributes excessive-augmentation instability to synthetic noise and longer-n degradation to value-estimation variance and inverse-dynamics errors (Sections 5.3-5.4; Appendices D-G). These introduce mechanisms and failure conditions beyond v2's accuracy/diversity discussion.

D1.justification: Appendices A-B add pseudocode, DiT and MLP architecture details, VP-SDE sampling settings, optimizer and training budgets, horizon, augmentation ratio, filter thresholds, four-A100 hardware information, and JAX-CORL baseline implementation details. v3 also adds statements about supplementary code and future public release; actual code availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for multi-step RL, DiT, VP-SDE, and JAX-CORL, and removes the Prudencio et al. offline-RL survey. Related-work prose is condensed, but the central positioning of bidirectional generation relative to prior augmentation methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 condenses related work, lightly edits methodological explanations, and reorganizes experimental subsections, moving Visualization from Section 5.3 to 5.5. It adds appendices and disclosure statements and revises author/header text. The abstract, introduction, conclusion, and overall main-text sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds a pipeline schematic, four analysis figures, Table 2, Appendix Tables S1-S8, and the tabulated Figure S1, substantially expanding the visual presentation. v2 Figure 1 is retained as v3 Figure 6 with a shortened caption. The conference template also changes the title page, headers, typography, and layout.

improvement.justification: The implementation details and new component studies make v2's framework more reproducible and empirically assessable. However, reporting problems limit the gains: v3 Table 1 retains an IQL Base average of 77.5 although its revised rows average 79.1, and identical BiTrajDiff DT task scores have conflicting averages of 73.7 and 71.8 in Tables S2 and S5. The documentation and diagnostic benefits support a net improvement, but these inconsistencies weaken the expanded performance evidence.
